 Order

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved with the award passed by the First Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Umaria in case No. 06/21 dated 21-08-2023 by which the injured claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was allowed and Rs. 18,96,109/- were awarded in favour of the claimants with interest @ 6% and Insurance Company was directed to pay the compensation amount.

2. In nutshell the claim case before the Tribunal was that on 26-01-2020, the injured claimant was returning from his school after Republic day Parade on the motor-cycle of her uncle, when they reached near Ghangrinaka, the driver of the offending vehicle of trailer No. MP-19HA-1032 registered in the name of M/s. Samman Transport driving the vehicle rashly and negligently hit behind the motor-cycle in which the claimant was travelling, as a result of which, the claimant fell down from the motor-cycle and her left hand came under the wheel of the trailer and her hand was badly injured.
First-aid was provided in District Hospital Umaria and from there she was referred to Jabalpur and from Jabalpur she was referred to Nagpur where she was treated.
3. In this case, the vehicle owner and driver denied the claim averments.

4 . The Insurance Company also denied the fact and had taken the defence that the offending vehicle was being driven in contravention of the terms and conditions of the policy and hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to compensate the claimant.
The Tribunal after framing issues, recorded the evidence of parties passed by the impugned award.

5. The Insurance Company has filed the appeal on the ground that the claimant has not examined any person to prove the discharge certificate, medical bills and in that situation, they cannot be treated to be proved.
On that basis, claimant was not eligible for the compensation in lieu of the said medical bills.

The doctor who deposed in support of the claimant Dr. Ruhela clearly stated that the disability certificate is a temporary and for 5 years only and also admitted that it was in relation to a particular organ and not regarding the entire body.
The Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs. 4 lacs against the disability.

The Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs. 4 lacs in the head of future treatment and expenses whereas no doctor evidence has been given in support of the future treatment and this amount has been awarded on the basis of speculation.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs 1 lacs for physical and mental pain whereas the claimant is only eligible to get Rs. 25,000/- in respect to that.

The Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs. 1,39,290/- for the travel expenses whereas from the statement of Nilima Rai (AW-1), it is clear that she was travelling in vehicle of Prahlad Rai and stated that she is not aware of the fact that the what her uncle was charging for the transportation.

She is also admitted that fare of Jabalpur to Nagpur is Rs. 200/- and if it is assumed to be true, she has travelled 13 times to Nagpur and two more people has accompanied her then maximum fare cannot be upto Rs. 7200/-.
The Tribunal has awarded excessive amount which is illegal, arbitrary and contrary to law.
6. Learned counsel for the claimant has supported the award passed by the Claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: 7. I have gone through the record.
8. The accident is not challenged before this Court hence, this Court is not appreciating the evidence regarding the accident.

Furthermore, from the FIR Ex. P/3, Charge-sheet, Ex. P/2, Injury Report Ex.
P/5 and statement of witnesses on behalf of the applicant.
The conclusion of the Claims Tribunal regarding accident and rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle MP- 19HA-1032 is affirmed.
9 . The Insurance Company has challenged the award on the head of medical expenses.
From the record, it is clear that on the date of accident, as per Ex. P/5, the victim was brought to District Hospital Umaria where she was examined.
She was also treated at Shalby Hospital, Jabalpur from 26-01-2020 to 04-02-2020 and from 07-02-2020 to 09-03-2020 in Sparsh Clinic, which is supported by the record of the hospital.

1 0 . Furthermore, on 04-05-2020 to 12-05-2020, she was admitted in Kingsway Hospital Nagpur and she travelled i.e. supported by the document Ex P/147 and these documents have not been challenged by the Insurance Company nor the documents were verified by the Insurance Company and on that these documents were found to be forged.
Hence, on the basis of above documents on record, the Claims Tribunal has awarded an actual amount incurred in the treatment by the claimant.
11. The next ground that has been challenged by the Insurance Company that the Claims Tribunal has awarded much higher amount in the head of conveyance from Umaria to Nagpur.
I have gone through the documents.

The documents of travel at the time when accident has happened are after 15-03- 2020, due to prevention of spreading of Corona Virus, the Government has put a lockdown and no public transport was available at that time.
Furthermore, no one can travel without the permission of competent authority.

In support of travel, the claimant has annexed the travel permission from village Baderi Umaria to Nagpur by Sub-Divisional Magistrate Bandhavgarh Umaria annexed with Ex. P/162, Ex. P/163 annexed with Ex. P/164, Ex.P/165, Ex. P/166, Ex.P/167 and Ex. P/168.
Furthermore, these visits from the OPD receipts, and the prescription of the concerned doctors.

In pass issued by the competent authority to travel during lockdown No. of the vehicle is MP-54-CA-0923A is clearly mentioned and in the cross-examination, the claimant has in paragraph-6 of the cross-examination has stated that the vehicle belongs to Dashairaj R/o- Khaira which is in relation to her Fufaji, she is not aware of the fare which the vehicle owner was charging for the conveyance.

Thus, the bills are supported by the passes to travel during Pandemic, the medical prescriptions of the doctors at Nagpur and that time, the public conveyance was not possible and there was no option but, to travel by private car
and on that basis conveyance charges awarded in favour of the claimant cannot be said to be excessive.

12. On the head of disability, the claimant-Nilima (AW-1) has stated that in the accident, the left hand came under the wheel of the trailer and veins, bones, muscular part were badly damaged and she is unable to perform any work from that hand and her hand is not working from elbow to fingers.

She has further stated that her further treatment had taken at Ganga Medical Hospital Coimbatore, Tamilnadu, for that purpose on 07-02-2011 she consulted the doctor of the hospital United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Ku. Nilima Rai on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13712243/
3 and obtained the estimate of expenditure of future surgery in which the doctor has estimated Rs.
3,50,000/- for the hospital bills, they had to bear the transportation charges and further states that these charges are amount of surgery for first round and she underwent multiple surgery and this fact has not been challenged in the cross-examination.
13.

sentences.text: Dr. L.N. Ruhela (AW-3) has stated that on 19-11-2020, the disability certificate Ex. P/1 was issued.
He has further stated that claimant suffered the crush injury in the left hand and in that hand 70% disability was found.

In cross- examination, he has admitted that this certificate is valid for 5 years and after 5 years, the patient will be further examined and on that basis, permanent disability certificate will be issued.

He has further stated that if the treatment is provided in higher centers, the disability may be reduced and he also admitted that the disability of 70% is in respect of particular organ and not in respect of the whole body.
14.

The claimant's father Narmada Prasad Rai(AW-2) has stated that on the advise of Dr. Shailesh Nisal, he went to Ganga Hospital, Coimbatore, Tamilnadu where the doctor after examination of the claimant has opined that by operating twice or thrice, the movement may come in the hand and in the first round of operation the expenditure may be Rs 3,50,000/- and he has submitted the documents to that effect.
15. I have gone through the record Ex. P/170 to Ex. P/172 of the Ganga Hospital and the disability certificate Ex.P/1.The

Claims Tribunal has assessed the disability in the left hand as 40% in respect of the whole body and the Claims Tribunal has also considered the other factors like discharge card,
summary of hospital Ex. P/5, Ex.P/6, Ex.P/14, Ex.P/60, Ex.P/144 to Ex.P/146 and on that basis concluded that she suffered 40% disability in respect of whole body and awarded compensation of Rs. 4 lacs on that head and further awarded an amount as estimated by the doctors of Ganga Hospital Coimbatore and considering the charges of the first surgery that cannot be said to be unreasonable.

16. Looking to the period of hospitalisation, her travel for the medical treatment from Umaria to Nagpur, Umaria to Coimbatore and the period for which she was treated as indoor patient and surgery conducted upon her, the amount awarded for the mental pain and suffering cannot be said to be excessive.
1 7 . After all considerations, the ground raised by the Insurance Company are without substance hence, the award of the Claims Tribunal is affirmed.
The appeal is dismissed.
The appellant shall bear the cost of respondents also.
18. With the copy of the order, the record of the Claims Tribunal be returned back.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE PG United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Ku. Nilima Rai on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13712243/
